BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to encouraging kindergarten outreach; amending RCW28A.150.205; adding a new section to chapter 28A.305 RCW; and creatinga new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds that the foundationsof school success are laid long before students enter kindergarten.Parents are their children's primary educators and must be acknowledgedas key partners in the education process. The legislature recognizesthat time and finances are constraints in expanding parent outreach andparent involvement activities. But the legislature believes that thebenefits of outreach to parents of kindergarten students and supportingtheir students' transition into school are worth the cost of someinstructional time in kindergarten.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 28A.305RCW to read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) A school district may submit an application to the state boardof education to count hours of kindergarten outreach as defined by this p. 1 HB 2586section for up to five percent of the minimum instructional hours forkindergarten students required under RCW 28A.150.220 and 28A.150.315. (2) The purpose of kindergarten outreach is to encourage, support,and assist parents in their role as the primary educator of theirchildren and to support students' successful transition into the K12education system. Outreach activities should be structured to be asaccessible as possible to the maximum number of parents. Participationin kindergarten outreach activities is optional for parents. (3) As used in this section, "kindergarten outreach" includes, butis not limited to: (a) Visits to students' homes to meet with parents or legalguardians; (b) Special educational events or activities for both parents andstudents; and (c) Classes or workshops for parents. (4) The state board of education shall develop a procedure forreceiving and reviewing applications under this section. A schooldistrict may submit an application for some or all kindergartenprograms in the district and for halfday or fullday kindergartenprograms. At a minimum: (a) Each application must include home visits as one kindergartenoutreach activity but may include other additional activities. (b) The type of kindergarten outreach activities proposed, theirintended purpose, and the estimated number of hours for each must beidentified and described in the application. (c) Kindergarten outreach must be conducted by the certificatedinstructional staff and classified instructional support staff whowould otherwise be providing direct instruction to the kindergartenstudents. Other school or district staff may also participate inoutreach activities. (5) An application approved by the state board of education underthis section may be in effect for no more than three school years,after which a school district must reapply.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 28A.150.205 and 1992 c 141 s 502 are each amended toread as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Unless the context clearly requires otherwise, the definition in HB 2586 p. 2 this section applies throughout RCW 28A.150.200 through 28A.150.295 andsection 2 of this act. (1) "Instructional hours" means those hours students are providedthe opportunity to engage in educational activity planned by and underthe direction of school district staff, as directed by theadministration and board of directors of the district, inclusive ofintermissions for class changes, recess, and teacher/parentguardianconferences that are planned and scheduled by the district for thepurpose of discussing students' educational needs or progress, andexclusive of time actually spent for meals. (2) For school districts with applications approved by the stateboard of education under section 2 of this act, "instructional hours"also means hours of kindergarten outreach activities.
